eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent drier conditions forecast by Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) are the main driver behind trader expectations for a highest temperature of 32–33°C on August 3, 2026.** Issued on July 31, the advisory highlights the first fortnight of August under the prevailing Southwest Monsoon, with fair and occasionally windy conditions expected to limit widespread cloud cover and reduce rainfall. This setup favors stronger daytime solar heating, pushing daily maxima to 33–34°C on most days—well above the long-term August average of about 31°C.

Supporting large-scale factors include developing El Niño conditions and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), both linked to warmer, drier weather across the Maritime Continent through reduced moisture convergence and suppressed convection. These climate influences align with the market's implied probabilities, where 32°C leads at 41.5% and 33°C follows at 30.5%, while 34°C or higher remains a lower-probability outcome at just 6%. Brief localized thundery showers in the afternoon could provide minor cooling on some days, helping explain the solid weighting on 31°C (20.5%) and the limited odds for extremes.

Traders appear to be weighting the official NEA outlook and broader seasonal signals heavily, with the next short-range model updates or daily observations likely to refine resolution odds as August 3 approaches.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus centers on 32–34°C maxima for Karachi on August 3, with 33°C holding the strongest implied probability at 40%.** Long-term August climatology for the coastal city shows average highs near 32°C, moderated by consistent Arabian Sea breezes and monsoon moisture that limit extreme heating. Recent Pakistan Meteorological Department guidance highlights strong sea breezes (40–55 km/h) and pleasant daytime temperatures of 29–31°C through the coming days, keeping the upper end of the distribution (35°C+) at low single-digit probabilities. Forecast models reflect this baseline, with any upward shift toward 34°C likely tied to temporary reductions in cloud cover or breeze strength rather than broader heat buildup. New observational data and updated runs from regional models will refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
